reviews.weakest: 4: The linked software exists and many mechanics check out, but "any computer," "any AI," "works the same way," and "free for everyone" outrun the supported platforms, Copilot requirement, and validation needed for generated Python agents.
reviews.fix:
Replace steps 5 and 6 with:
  • Make your own.Ask an AI to adapt the exported file for one chore you repeat. Save only the Python code in a file ending in _agent.py, then drag it onto Brainstem. Continue only if Brainstem says it installed successfully and the new agent appears in the agent list; test it with one real request.
  • Hand it on.Export the tested agent and send it to a friend who already has Brainstem. They install it and run the same request to verify it on their computer. Or submit the tested file to the registry.

reviews.weakest: 4: step 5 promises 'It uses it on your next message' and 'No coding' for an AI-written Python file, but the Brainstem's own importer asks you to confirm, rejects files that do not load and renames them (the page says none of this), and 'about ten minutes each', 'people say' and the footer's 'Wildhaven Homes LLC' (the licences name a person, not the LLC) cannot be confirmed from any linked source.
reviews.fix:
Replace steps 4 and 5 so nobody has to open, name or save a .py file (Export already downloads it and the importer adds _agent.py itself):
  • Read an agent.Click Export next to ManageMemory. Your browser saves a small file called manage_memory_agent.py, usually in Downloads. Drag it into an AI chat you already use and ask: Explain this in plain words.
  • Make your own.In the same chat, ask: Write me a new agent just like this one, for a chore I repeat, as a .py file I can download. Drag that file onto your Brainstem window and click OK when it asks (an agent is a small program, so accept only files you trust). It uses it on your next message. If it says the agent did not load, paste that message into the chat and ask for a fix.
